source.text: The search box on the notes list of example-web

checks.title: Find where the list is drawn
checks.why: The search box filters what this function draws.

do.text: Open the list module and find `drawList`
do.see: A function that returns one row per note

checks.passes: You can point at the line that builds each row.
checks.nothingFromHere: Reading code is yours to do.
checks.more: Every filter ends up calling this one function, so it is the best place to start reading.

teach.what: drawList takes the typed word and returns the rows whose text contains it.

idea.text: A filter is a loop that keeps what matches.

teach.why: Knowing this makes the search box easy to change later.

edge.text: Call it with an empty word

checks.title: See how typing reaches the filter
checks.why: The box calls the filter on every keystroke.

do.see: It rewrites the list from the box value

checks.passes: You can say what happens when a letter is typed.
checks.nothingFromHere: Reading code is yours to do.

teach.what: onInput reads the box value and redraws the list through drawList.

idea.text: An input handler is a small function wired to a key press.

edge.see: The list always matches the box

checks.title: Know what Escape does
checks.why: Escape is the shortcut that undoes a search.

do.see: Escape empties the box and redraws

checks.passes: You can say what Escape does to the box.
checks.nothingFromHere: Reading code is yours to do.

teach.what: onKey clears the box on Escape, then runs onInput again.
